skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Guides agents to run fresh verification commands before claiming work is complete, fixed, or ready for commit.
skill.summary: Requires fresh verification evidence before claiming work is complete.
skill.author: Cycleaddict

content.value_statement: Completion claims often happen before tests, builds, or requirements are actually checked. This skill forces fresh evidence before any success statement.
actual_capabilities: Requires identifying the evidence needed for each success claim.
Directs agents to run fresh, complete verification commands.
Encourages reading full output and exit status before reporting.
Covers tests, lint, builds, regression checks, requirements, and delegated work.
Separates verified claims from unverified gaps.
limitations: Does not execute commands by itself; the host agent must run them.
Does not define project-specific test or build commands.
Cannot prove correctness beyond the selected verification scope.
May add time to small tasks where evidence is still required.

use_cases.title: Prevent premature completion claims
use_cases.description: Require fresh test, build, or checklist evidence before reporting a task as done.

use_cases.title: Review AI coding work
use_cases.description: Check delegated agent output against diffs, requirements, and verification results before accepting success.

use_cases.title: Standardize handoff discipline
use_cases.description: Create a consistent evidence standard for commits, pull requests, and task updates.

prompt_templates.title: Basic completion check
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before saying a small task is done.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before you say this task is complete, identify the verification command, run it, read the output, and report only what the output proves.

prompt_templates.title: Full change verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a code change that may affect tests or builds.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the verification-before-completion process on this change. Check tests, lint, build, and requirements before making any completion claim.

prompt_templates.title: Requirement checklist audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a task has multiple stated requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this implementation against the plan. Create a verification checklist, run each relevant check, and separate proven results from remaining gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Regression proof review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for bug fixes that need red-green evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this regression fix, perform red-green verification. Confirm the test fails without the fix, passes with it restored, and report exact evidence.

output_examples.input: The agent is ready to say a validation bug is fixed.
output_examples.output: I reran the failing validation test. It now passes with zero failures, so the bug fix is verified.

output_examples.input: The agent wants to claim the build passes without a fresh run.
output_examples.output: I cannot claim the build passes yet. I need to run the full build and read the result first.

output_examples.input: A delegated agent reports success on a requested change.
output_examples.output: I checked the diff and verified the requested file changed. One requirement remains unverified, so completion is not proven yet.

best_practices: Choose the command that directly proves the claim.
Run full verification after the final relevant change.
Report failures and gaps with the same visibility as passes.
anti_patterns: Claiming success from memory, confidence, or earlier runs.
Treating lint, tests, and build as interchangeable evidence.
Accepting a delegated agent report without checking the diff and result.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before any claim that work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for review.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the host agent to choose and run the right verification commands.

faq.question: Can prior test results count as evidence?
faq.answer: Usually no. The skill requires fresh verification after the relevant work is complete.

faq.question: What if the verification command fails?
faq.answer: Report the failure clearly, include what was checked, and do not claim completion.

faq.question: Does this replace project-specific quality gates?
faq.answer: No. It reinforces those gates by requiring evidence before success claims.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is tool-neutral and supports agent workflows across those environments.
